reviews.title: Paywalls and weird formatting.
reviews.text:
I’ve been getting back into the grind of learning Japanese, so I decided to try this app. The first two courses were great, they were easy to understand, and if I made mistakes I could get an explanation on where I went wrong. However, the explanation feature suddenly got paywalled after a few courses. There was also a point where I was stuck on a lesson not because I got the material wrong, because I was formatting it incorrectly. I had to spend nearly 20  minutes just to figure out where I went wrong with my formatting because the explanation was paywalled and you have to pay $20 (USD) to have access to the explanation feature. That is a lot of money for me, and I wish more language learning apps would make learning more accessible for people who don’t have money to throw at a monthly subscription.  After just five lessons, you’re suddenly blocked from the sixth lesson without a subscription, you can skip that lesson, but you can’t do the 7th lesson which is a test that’s required to continue.

The app was also inaccessible to those who need larger screens. It was not adjusted so the keyboard was covering text that was important to read. (You cannot simply slide down the keyboard to read and then re-enable it. It senses any kind of tap or slide as an answer so you would be accidentally submitting something without answering it.) reviews.title: Japanese
reviews.text: I may be in the minority but I do not enjoy the app. It’s catered to people who are on their phones all day, which am I not and can’t be. As a western speaker, it attempts to appeal to your ability to pronounce certain words. Which then in turn ends up messing up your pronunciation of them. “SA” in Japanese is pronounced “SO” (according to the app) but then, “SHI” is pronounced “Shee” but then “SO” is pronounced “SO”. Then when you put the vowels together It’s just not the way Japanese is pronounced when using English to sound out Japanese Kanji. I paid out right for it. You get what you get. Hire a tutor.

reviews.title: Don’t buy lifetime subscription before understanding the limitations
reviews.text:
Don’t buy the lifetime subscription before understanding what you’re getting into. There’s no discount if you decide to upgrade to platinum from premium, which they will push you to. The only way to understand why your answer is wrong is in Platinum subscription. Other than that, you are paying for an expensive set of flash cards with no direction when you need help.

I bought lifetime Premium membership and it had the ‘explain my answer’ feature working. They now took it away and are pushing you to buy Platinum to use it. 

I like how the app is organized but you get very basic lessons that are not enough to use the app as the only source. The ‘explain my answer’ feature helped mitigate that, but now they are following the path of Duolingo where they want you to buy higher tiers. At least Duolingo now tells you why your answer is wrong. I already regret buying the lifetime subscription.

reviews.title: False advertising
reviews.text: The AI that they claim can chat with you can only do so under your specific scenario settings. Basically you choose what role you want the AI to play and what role you will play and then it has a conversation with you. No explanation of the japanses used no switching between languages to explain anything it's really bad and not good for a beginner. I asked for a refund they denied and they let me know that their decision is final so I'm letting others know that it's a scam, don't pay for the premium for the AI chat, its not worth it, I will do some real videos of it in action for social media asap.
